meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with commercial law principles significantly influenced by Common Law trust jurisprudence in foundation law

Panama–Republic of Korea Bilateral Investment Treaty
Agreement between Panama and Germany on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments
Agreement between Panama and France on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (as amended), principally Articles 6-12 (creation, endowment, registration and legal personality), 18-23 (Foundation Council, officers and beneficiaries) and 30 (Protector); supplemented by the General Rules of the Public Registry and the resident-agent AML framework of Law No. 23 of 2015 and its Executive Decrees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), General Directorate, Private Interest Foundations Registration Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter), executed as a notarized public deed (Escritura Pública) before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed with the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum endowment is fixed in Law No. 25 of 1995; the market-standard declared initial endowment (dotación inicial) is US$10,000. No escrow deposit or immediate paid-in proof is required at filing; the founder signs an endowment declaration and the contribution may be completed by supplementary notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME] (dated ______). The undersigned members, constituting the initial Foundation Council, unanimously resolve: (1) to accept the founder's declaration of the initial endowment; (2) to adopt the registered office located at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and to confirm the Resident Agent appointed by the founder; (3) to install the Council, appointing [Name] as Chair and [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer; (4) to authorize opening bank accounts, maintaining accounting records, and executing contracts for logistics-fleet route optimization and telematics software; (5) to direct the Resident Agent to pay all statutory fees and complete registration with the Public Registry of Panama; and (6) to adopt the Foundation Rules. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Reservation, and AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá online pre-inscription desk (SEDE portal) in coordination with the licensed Resident Agent, an AML-obligated subject under Law No. 23 of 2015.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed foundation name for availability verification and optional reservation through the Registry's online services or via the Resident Agent; concurrently deliver to the Resident Agent the complete KYC packet (identification, references, source of funds, and beneficial-ownership statement) so that the statutory due-diligence file is completed before charter execution.
required_dossiers: Completed name search/reservation form
Passport copies of the founder, Foundation Council members, and identified beneficiaries
Bank or professional reference letters
Source-of-funds declaration
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, resubmit with three alternate names; if an AML inquiry arises, supply supplementary evidence within five working days; any KYC deficiency must be cured before execution of the charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública) before a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría del Circuito (Notary Public) of the Republic of Panama engaged by the Resident Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review and finalize the Acta Constitutiva, including foundation name, purpose, initial endowment, term, Foundation Council, Protector, registered office, Resident Agent appointment, and foundation rules. The Founder and founding Council members execute the deed before the notary; the notary retains the original in protocol and issues certified testimonies for registration. Pay notary fees and obtain at least one clean first testimony for the Registry.
required_dossiers: Final draft Acta Constitutiva
Resident Agent's notarized AML file
Passport copies of founder and Council members
Written acceptance letters of the Council members
Endowment declaration signed by the founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, amend the draft and re-execute by addendum before filing; no registry penalty applies if the instrument is corrected prior to presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Charter with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, General Directorate, Private Interest Foundations Section; payment at the Registry cashier or via SEDE electronic payment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first testimonio of the Escritura Pública together with two reproductions, the Resident Agent's acceptance and idoneidad (license), and the official fee payment receipt (approximately US$100). The Registry assigns an entry number (asiento), verifies the instrument, and issues the inscription certificate; legal personality of the foundation arises upon registration.
required_dossiers: First testimonio (certified copy) of the executed Escritura Pública
Two reproductions of the testimonio
Resident Agent license and acceptance letter
Proof of payment of registry fees
Cover letter of the responsible attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns a reiteración (query), respond in writing within ten working days through the reiteration procedure, pay the corresponding fee, and for material defects execute a supplemental public deed to cure the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certified Registry Evidence and Post-Registration Endorsements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Certification Section (Sección de Certificaciones).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order the certified inscription certificate and a certified copy of the inscribed charter; verify the exact legal name, date, and inscription number; request a certification of no impairment if required for banking purposes; distribute certified copies to the Resident Agent and legal counsel.
required_dossiers: Inscription entry number
Reference number of the foundation file at the Registry
Payment vouchers for certification fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors are cured by an administrative correction request (fé de enmienda) submitted with the registry file; substantial errors require a new decision by the registry official within ten working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Administrative and Fiscal Activation (RUC, Municipal Notices, and Bank Account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; Alcaldía de Panamá (Municipal Treasury); licensed Panamanian banks.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the foundation will hold Panamanian-source assets or execute local contracts, register with the DGI to obtain a RUC; otherwise the territorial-income exemption applies. Monitor and pay the flat annual foundation franchise tax as scheduled, file the municipal Aviso de Operación for any physical office, and open the corporate bank account presenting the certified charter and the Foundation Council's banking resolutions.
required_dossiers: Certified inscription certificate of the Registry
RUC application form
Identity documents of the Council members and signatories
Foundation tax payment schedule
Bank account application and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For DGI objections, correct and re-file the RUC application electronically within five working days; for bank rejection, provide an updated source-of-funds file and alternative signatory structure or reapply at another licensed bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ISIC 6201 (software and telematics services). If a physical office is maintained, the local permitting body is the Alcaldía de Panamá (Tesorería Municipal), and the sectoral reference for commercial activities is the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), General Directorate of Industry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory national operating license applies to the telematics SaaS model (requires_statutory_license=false). A municipal Aviso de Operación is administratively required only for the physical registered office, together with a fire-safety inspection certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Directorate of Environmental Impact Evaluation; engaged primarily for landlord or financing requirements.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category I not triggered; office-based software activity without industrial installation, combustion, or process discharge, so no Environmental Impact Assessment report or registration dossier is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or point-source emissions. General obligations: municipal sewer and solid-waste compliance under Law No. 8 of 2006 (General Waste Law); end-of-life IT hardware managed under the RAEE regulation (Resolución AG-0325-2014); carbon-footprint reporting is voluntary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá – annual fire-safety inspection certificate for the office premises; Alcaldía de Panamá certificate of use and occupancy for the leased office; MITRADEL (Ministry of Labor) workplace-safety registration for any personnel; SINAPROC civil-protection and evacuation plan posted for the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; primary e-portals: TribuNet (https://tribunet.mef.gob.pa) and Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa); e-invoicing platform administered by DGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF), including the PA_PIF fleet-dispatch logistics SaaS structure, must procure a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) from the DGI. Procedure: (1) Appoint a Panamanian resident agent and, where taxable activity will occur, a fiscal representative; (2) file and register the foundation charter (notarized deed and, if used abroad, apostilled/certified translation) with the Public Registry of Panama; (3) obtain the registered official corporate documents and the resolution identifying the foundation council; (4) apply for RUC online via TribuNet or at a DGI service window, submitting foundation documents, identity of council members, stated business activity (ISIC 6201 / logistics technology), local address, and fiscal agent letter; (5) register for ITBMS in the same RUC dossier and select the monthly/quarterly filing period; (6) obtain the digital tax certificate / electronic signature for Sede Electrónica and e-invoicing. The RUC is the unified TIN/VAT ID; no separate NIT is issued to legal entities. A purely passive offshore PIF with no Panama-source transactions may remain unregistered only if it performs no Panamanian taxable activities, but commercial SaaS operations with Panamanian customers require active RUC registration before invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no domestic 'check-the-box' or pass-through election equivalent to US Treasury Regulations §301.7701-3; the PIF is a juridical person subject to entity-level taxation on Panama-source income only and is not transparent. There is no statutory hybrid-match election under Panama fiscal law; classification effects are determined by each foreign jurisdiction. On the domestic side, a small taxpayer may opt for the simplified/accelerated regime under DGI rules, and an enterprise may elect to register under the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime or Panama Pacífico special economic-zone regime if it satisfies the applicable substance conditions, but these elections are not entity classification elections and are not available to a pure PIF absent qualifying activity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a value-added consumption tax, with selected services also subject to municipal business tax (Industria y Comercio).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 0 (no minimum turnover threshold for registration). Under the Panamanian Fiscal Code, any person habitually selling movable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register as an ITBMS taxpayer before engaging in the activity; the first taxable supply or importation triggers the obligation. A special simplified regime for small taxpayers may reduce compliance mechanics but does not exempt registration from the DGI/RUC system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing applies, on a phased basis, to DGI-registered taxpayers, including SaaS and logistics-telematics operators. Invoices must be generated in the DGI-approved XML format, signed with a digital certificate issued by an authorized Panamanian certification authority, and transmitted to the DGI's Sistema de Facturación Electrónica in near real time for validation and assignment of a fiscal authorization (electronic stamping/QR code). Offline issuance is permitted only for limited pre-authorized periods, with transmission within 24 hours. The printed representation must contain the QR code, DGI authorization, RUC, and series number; paper invoices without electronic authorization are invalid for ITBMS credit and customer deductibility. The DGI may require data-exchange APIs or certified billing providers for high-volume filers; the logistics/dispatch business must integrate its Stripe Billing and invoice flows with the Panamanian e-invoicing gateway for all Panama-taxable transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) is claimable when tangible goods are physically exported from Panama under a customs exit declaration and title/risk passes to a non-resident buyer. For offshore services (including fleet-route optimization and real-time telematics SaaS), zero-rating / tax exclusion is available when the service is rendered for the benefit of a non-resident counterparty and is effectively used, consumed, or exploited outside Panama; mere billing to a foreign entity is insufficient. The provider must be able to prove the non-resident nature of the recipient, the offshore use/benefit, and actual receipt of payment from abroad. Creditable input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated supplies may be refunded or carried forward, but export refund claims are specifically audited for substance and documentary support.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated customs export declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera or equivalent DGI/ANAM electronic filing) showing the PA_PIF/RUC as exporter and the foreign destination
Bill of Lading, airway bill, CIM/SMGS rail or equivalent international transport document evidencing physical departure from Panamanian customs territory
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, packing list describing the goods/software and the non-resident buyer
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement showing foreign-source payment received within the repatriation window
Signed service agreement or SaaS master agreement demonstrating the non-resident beneficiary, offshore use/consumption, and transfer of risk for logistics/telematics services
DGI zero-rating declaration/export service form or certification, if and when requested by the DGI for processing an export refund or input-credit claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is strictly construed. If the DGI determines that no valid export occurred, that payment was not repatriated within 180 days, or that an offshore-service classification was artificial or unsupported, it will retroactively reassess ITBMS at the standard 7% rate on the gross transaction, add monthly late-payment interest and late-filing surcharges, deny input credits and export refunds, and impose statutory fines tied to the omitted tax (which for fraudulent statements may reach or approximate 100% of the tax). False claims of export or foreign-source revenue can also trigger criminal tax-evasion exposure under Panamanian law, debarment from DGI authorized-issuer/e-invoicing status, and, where banking AML reporting is concerned, STR/FIU referral. The taxpayer bears the burden of proof and must retain the complete customs, contract, log, telematics-use, and banking record set for at least the Panamanian limitation period (extended to the applicable statute of limitations when fraud is alleged).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama maintains a fully dollarized monetary system. The Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the National Government and banker for public revenues; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the prudential regulator of all banking activities. There is no national central bank issuing monetary policy or administering foreign-exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian balboa is legal tender only as token coinage and exists as a unit of account; the United States dollar is legal tender for all transactions and freely circulates. Panama imposes no foreign-exchange control regime, no prior approval requirement, and no capital or current account convertibility restriction. Profit remittance is therefore free. Dividends from Panama-source income may attract the 5% dividend tax unless taxed under the alternate calculation of payable taxes, while foreign-source income is outside the Panamanian territorial income tax base. No overseas remittance tax or exchange surrender requirement applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds to a central authority. Exporters may retain all foreign-currency receipts in Panamanian banks, in US dollars or other convertible currencies, and no mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline exists. Export documentation must nevertheless be maintained for customs and for validation of the territorial-source income exemption.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Collection Account; Escrow Account for Investor Capital
Fiscal Agency and Low-Cost Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account for Government or Regulated Contractual Inflows
Commercial Banking Operational Account; International Payments and Trade Credit Facilities
Multi-Currency Operational Account; Corporate Card and Merchant Services; Segregated Escrow Account
State-Development Operational Account and Collateral Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to moderate. An offshore digital EMI cannot be used as the principal treasury banking relationship because it lacks a Panama SBP banking or e-money license and does not provide locally regulated clearing or depositor protection. Panama requires any entity holding customer funds or providing payments to be authorized as a bank, finance company, or registered payment processor. Relevant EU or UK EMIs may be used as supplementary disbursement channels for small-value SaaS subscriptions, but all statutory and core liquidity flows should reside in SBP-licensed Panamanian banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Panamanian Private Interest Foundation must satisfy risk-based KYC rules. Directors, foundation council members, and ultimate beneficial owners must submit certified passports, public registry extracts, foundation charter and bylaws, and a sworn beneficial-ownership statement. Physical presence of all signatories is not a uniform SBP mandate, but in practice a face-to-face interview or secure video KYC appointment is required by many commercial banks. Remote opening is viable for low-risk corporate structures where a licensed Panamanian counsel, trustee, or registered agent confirms identity and where the final signatory provides a notarized and apostilled acceptance of account terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation anonymity and perceived lack of a transparent beneficial-ownership statement during bank onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled foundation registration certificate; foundation charter and endowment; bylaws; current registry extract; beneficial-ownership declaration identifying each council member, protector if any, and the ultimate individual owner; board resolutions appointing signatories and setting dual-signature authority; valid identification documents and proof of address of all parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No material corporate substance for a Panama-registered PIF engaged in international logistics technology services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panama office lease or co-working arrangement; evidence of local administrative staff or contracted Panamanian administrator; audited or management-prepared financial statements; real commercial invoices from fleet customers; insurance policies; board minutes approving material contracts and treasury mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions or negative-news hits arising from freight routing and fleet-dispatch counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written OFAC and EU sanctions screening policy and denial-list procedures; completed counterparty due-diligence file for each client, vendor, and end customer; fleet route mapping confirming no business with comprehensively sanctioned territories; customs and maritime compliance evidence for all vessels or vehicles; adverse-media search reports with analytic justification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for high-volume inbound technology subscription revenue and investor capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment processor settlement reports and merchant-of-record statements; audited or accountant-reviewed revenue schedule; tax filings supporting territorial-source exemption; investor subscription agreements and source-of-funds evidence; commercial contracts with customers; bank reference letters from reputable foreign banks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound investor capital should be routed via SWIFT MT103 or equivalent USD wire to the Panamanian commercial bank account under the legal name of the foundation. The payment narrative should state Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF or an equivalent unambiguous purpose-of-payment code. The receiving bank may require a foundation council resolution, subscription agreement, bank reference, and source-of-funds KYC evidence. Non-USD capital should be converted into USD at the receiving bank's spot rate using a plain, freely executable FX transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring logistics SaaS and fleet-management fees, use SWIFT MT103 to execute high-value payments to vendors and overseas subsidiaries. For large fleet procurement or trade-related settlements, use a commercial letter of credit issued by an SBP-licensed bank and confirmed or advised by the seller's bank under UCP600. For low-value subscription collections, use Stripe Billing card and ACH/SEPA settlement rails with automatic treasury reconciliation. All outbound disbursements must be matched to invoices, screened against sanctions and denial lists, and documented for income-tax territorial-source analysis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts in USD/EUR, USD/GBP, and USD/CNH booked with SBP-authorized Panamanian commercial banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term EUR or GBP financing hedged against USD cash flows
Non-deliverable forward contracts executed through international banking counterparties for Latin American currencies where local deliverable liquidity is unavailable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Government Tax (Impuesto Único de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 December of each calendar year; not tied to anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% monthly surcharge plus statutory interest under the Código Fiscal; failure to pay for more than 90 days can trigger administrative suspension of good standing, and continued non-payment may result in administrative strike-off from the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Registry Update (Reporte Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year; additional update required within 30 days of any change in beneficiaries, Foundation Council members, or founder's reserved rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines typically range from USD 100 to USD 500 per infraction; repeated failure to file or update beneficial ownership data can suspend the Foundation's legal standing before third parties and prevent issuance of certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Information Declaration for Panamanian-Source Income (Declaración Anual de Rentas) – applicable only if the Foundation generates Panama-source taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (calendar year ending 31 December); no filing is required for passive, foreign-source-only PIF income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the Código Fiscal range from 5% to 10% of assessed tax with a minimum of USD 50; chronic non-compliance may lead to presumptive tax assessments and suspension of the Foundation's tax identification certificate.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private Interest Foundations are not subject to a mandatory independent statutory audit. A certified audit is required only if the Foundation's by-laws (reglamento) explicitly mandate it, or if the Foundation carries on commercial activity within Panama and its annual gross Panamanian income exceeds USD 3,000,000, in which case the DGI-standard audit obligation applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian GAAP applied consistently; for foundations required to present financial statements to the DGI or by the terms of the foundation deed, IFRS as adopted by the Panamanian Association of Public Accountants applies. The Foundation must maintain internal accounting records sufficient to determine its financial position, but these are not publicly filed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 129 of 2020, requires each Private Interest Foundation to identify and maintain current beneficial ownership data with the Public Registry. Although PIFs do not issue shares or ‘shareholding transfers’, any substitution of the founder's rights, addition or removal of beneficiaries, or change in Foundation Council membership must be reported within 30 days. Additionally, every PIF must file or reconfirm its beneficial ownership declaration annually no later than 30 June, aligned with the annual PIF government tax cycle. The Foundation Council must ensure the registered agent has access to a current beneficiary register for inspection by competent authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Founder's Reserved Rights
Minute Book (Libro de Actas) and Resolutions Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – USD 1,000 per year for Panamanian resident agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required for passive PIFs; voluntary certified audit typically USD 2,500 – USD 8,000 depending on asset complexity and activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: foreign-source income (including international SaaS subscription fees from logistics-fleet dispatch software) is statutorily excluded from Panamanian taxable income, producing a 0% effective CIT rate for a genuinely offshore PIF. No exemption exists for Panama-source income; services rendered or economically utilized within Panama are taxed at 25%. The SEM (Multinational Headquarters) regime under Law 41 of 2007 may grant a preferential 0%-5% effective rate for qualifying centralized service functions subject to strict economic substance tests. Foreign tax credits are unavailable for Panamanian tax purposes because the territorial exclusion already removes foreign-source revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1210 - Declaración Anual de Impuesto Sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically via the DGI 'Panamá T@X' e-filing portal (eservices.dgi.gob.pa) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; supplemented by 12 monthly provisional income tax prepayments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year PIFs, no later than March 31 of the following year. The exact operative date is assigned by the DGI 'Calendario de Vencimientos' (Z-schedule) based on the last digit of the RUC taxpayer identification number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sales of goods and services, before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source gross revenue. Foreign-source subscription revenue must be omitted here and detailed in the Foreign-Source Income Annex (RFE) with supporting contracts and payment records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex RFE - Rentas de Fuente Extranjera
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Itemized schedule of foreign-source income claimed as territorially excluded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each foreign client, contracting jurisdiction, place of performance of services, server/hosting location, and the exact amount of revenue excluded. The economic activity must be verifiably performed outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions attributable to generating taxable gross income: direct operating costs, overhead, salaries, depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred to earn Panama-source income. Foreign-source costs should be allocated to the RFE annex and excluded from this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible items (e.g., under-documented related-party fees, non-withheld payments to non-residents).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF paid technical-service fees to a non-resident without 12.5% withholding, the payment must be added back and treated as nondeductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure offshore PIF, this line should equal zero only if the RFE annex fully substantiates the territorial exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory income tax resulting from applying 25% to Line 108.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% exclusively to Panama-source net income; no treaty or foreign-tax credit is granted at this stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 112 - Créditos y Pagos a Cuenta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: monthly provisional payments, withholding tax certificates, and any prior overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore PIFs with no Panama-source exposure typically have zero credits; if zero-filing, verify that the DGI has not auto-assessed minimum prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 115 - Saldo a Pagar o a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due or refund position after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the balance electronically through T@X. A zero-return for a PIF with exclusively foreign-source income is accepted only when the RFE annex is complete.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic fine from USD 50 to USD 4,000 depending on taxpayer category, plus a 5% per month (or fraction) surcharge on the tax due, capped at 50%. Late payment: 10% surcharge on the unpaid amount plus 1% monthly interest (Fiscal Code Arts. 712-718). Non-filing after official notice triggers RUC suspension, bank-account freezes, and cancellation of operating licenses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 155 - Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia; filed electronically via the DGI 'Panamá T@X' portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory window as Form 1210: within 3 months after fiscal year-end (by March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers, adjusted per the DGI Z-calendar by RUC last digit).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC, legal name, fiscal period, consolidated group status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory only if the PIF's annual related-party transactions reach or exceed USD 250,000; otherwise the form is not required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of related parties: founder, foundation council members, beneficiaries, and affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF, disclose the founder, each council member, every beneficiary with an entitlement exceeding 10%, and any affiliated logistics/technology entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature, amount, and counterparty for each controlled transaction (services, royalties, interest, cost allocations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report intercompany SaaS licensing or fleet-dispatch service fees in USD; segment by transaction type and counterparty jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's-length method selected for each transaction category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select one of the five Panama-recognized OECD methods and attach a one-page ALP conclusion memo.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sworn statement signed by the legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Foundation Council member signing the form assumes civil and criminal responsibility for the accuracy of the TP disclosures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing or late filing of Form 155: fines up to USD 10,000. Failure to substantiate controlled transactions enables the DGI to reassess at the 25% rate, add the 10% surcharge and 1% monthly interest, and deny corresponding deductions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends or distributions made from net tax-paid Panama-source profits (Fiscal Code Art. 733). Distributions of foreign-source income by a PIF to beneficiaries are outside Panama's territorial tax scope and bear 0% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's income tax treaties in force (Barbados, Czech Republic, France, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, UAE) typically reduce dividend WHT to 5% for substantial shareholdings (generally 10% or more) and 10%-15% for portfolio holdings. Administrative protocol: (1) the beneficial owner obtains a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction's competent authority, issued for the current or immediately preceding calendar year; (2) the TRC, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and the applicable treaty article claim are submitted to the Panamanian withholding agent before payment; (3) the payer retains the documentation for 5 years; (4) if the statutory 10% was withheld, the non-resident may claim a refund via a rectificatory return and TRC submission before the DGI within the 3-year tax prescription period (Art. 708, Fiscal Code).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical-assistance fees arising from intellectual property or services economically used in Panama: 12.5% statutory withholding on gross amounts paid to non-residents; treaty rates generally range from 5% to 10%. Interest paid to non-resident lenders: 0% Panamanian withholding under the territorial principle, provided the financing documentation is executed abroad and the lender maintains no permanent establishment in Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 250,000 (USD 250,000) in annual related-party transactions triggers the Form 155 TP informative return; PAB 2,500,000 (USD 2,500,000) in annual related-party transactions triggers a full Local File. An MNE group with consolidated worldwide gross revenue of USD 150,000,000 or more requires a Master File. CbC reporting obligations apply only to groups meeting the OECD EUR 750M threshold where the ultimate parent is resident in a jurisdiction with an activated exchange agreement with Panama; domestic CbC legislation is not yet operational.
